## Structure and components

- [statement] A tree test isolates category structure and text labels from visual layout and other contextual cues. Its results do not by themselves establish findability in the fully designed site, where design and search can change behavior. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/card-sorting-tree-testing-differences/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://measuringu.com/tree-testing-ia/, https://raw.studio/blog/card-sorting-and-tree-testing, https://www.nngroup.com/articles/interpreting-tree-test-results/
- [statement] Card-sort groupings and participant-created names are design inputs, not a ready-made navigation structure: researchers must interpret them and evaluate candidate hierarchies. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/card-sorting-tree-testing-differences/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/card-sorting-definition/, https://www.uxmatters.com/mt/archives/2007/09/card-sorting-mistakes-made-and-lessons-learned.php

## How it works

- [statement] NN/G cautions that predefined categories in hybrid sorts can bias participants toward similarly structured categories; it prefers tree testing over closed sorting when the goal is evaluating navigation categories. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/card-sorting-definition/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing
- [statement] Practitioner experience warns against treating every findability problem as a taxonomy problem: navigation controls and search quality may need attention even when card sorting is available. (medium confidence) — https://www.uxmatters.com/mt/archives/2007/09/card-sorting-mistakes-made-and-lessons-learned.php · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://measuringu.com/tree-testing-ia/

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use task paths to decide whether to rename, regroup, or provide multiple routes to content. ONRR’s tree test exposed competing category expectations and led the team to propose cross-listing resources and reorganizing categories. (low confidence) — https://digital.gov/2022/01/06/open-source-information-architecture-design-using-the-tools-you-have-to-conduct-card-sorting-and-tree-testing · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Define the accepted destinations for each tree-test task before interpreting success. Success counts participants who select a correct final location; visiting it and then choosing another location is failure. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/tree-testing/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/interpreting-tree-test-results/
- [statement] In ONRR’s card-sort case, a small sample spread across two audiences left some cards without a strong placement pattern; this is a case-specific sample limitation, not a universal participant threshold. (low confidence) — https://digital.gov/2022/01/06/open-source-information-architecture-design-using-the-tools-you-have-to-conduct-card-sorting-and-tree-testing · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing
- [statement] Limit task-learning effects: ONRR observed participants learning tree categories quickly and emphasized fewer tasks and randomized order; NN/G recommends assigning each participant only one tree version when comparing trees. (medium confidence) — https://digital.gov/2022/01/06/open-source-information-architecture-design-using-the-tools-you-have-to-conduct-card-sorting-and-tree-testing · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/tree-testing/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Treat card-sort patterns as input to a draft taxonomy, then evaluate its labels and hierarchy through tree testing and revise problematic branches. Sorting results require design judgment rather than automatic adoption as the final structure. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/card-sorting-tree-testing-differences/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://raw.studio/blog/card-sorting-and-tree-testing
- [statement] Use divergent navigation paths to consider cross-listing rather than forcing every item into one location. ONRR proposed cross-listing resources after participants split between plausible categories; NN/G recommends using observed demand rather than adding every theoretically possible placement. (medium confidence) — https://digital.gov/2022/01/06/open-source-information-architecture-design-using-the-tools-you-have-to-conduct-card-sorting-and-tree-testing · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/interpreting-tree-test-results/
- [statement] Use representative content and clear card labels, and examine audience differences rather than assuming all users organize information alike. In the ONRR case, researchers selected cards using usage and search data, analyzed audiences separately, and found unclear labels impeded sorting. (low confidence) — https://digital.gov/2022/01/06/open-source-information-architecture-design-using-the-tools-you-have-to-conduct-card-sorting-and-tree-testing · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing
- [statement] Pilot card labels and avoid repeated wording that encourages superficial word matching instead of meaningful grouping. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/card-sorting-definition/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Information architecture organizes content and labels to support finding information. Card sorting informs grouping and labeling decisions; it does not produce a complete navigation or search system. (medium confidence) — https://raw.studio/blog/card-sorting-and-tree-testing · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://www.uxmatters.com/mt/archives/2007/09/card-sorting-mistakes-made-and-lessons-learned.php
- [statement] Card sorting asks participants to group content items, revealing candidate organizations; tree testing asks participants to find destinations within a proposed hierarchy, evaluating findability. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/card-sorting-tree-testing-differences/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://raw.studio/blog/card-sorting-and-tree-testing, https://measuringu.com/tree-testing-ia/
- [statement] In an open card sort, participants create and name groups. In a closed sort, they assign cards to predefined categories. A hybrid sort supplies categories but permits participants to add their own. (medium confidence) — https://raw.studio/blog/card-sorting-and-tree-testing · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/card-sorting-definition/
- [statement] NN/G cautions that predefined categories in a hybrid sort can bias participants toward similarly structured categories, and recommends considering that format only in specific circumstances. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/card-sorting-definition/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing
- [statement] Pilot card labels and avoid wording that invites superficial word matching. Ambiguous labels can prevent placement: the ONRR team reported this problem and planned to revise labels before its closed sort. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/card-sorting-definition/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://digital.gov/2022/01/06/open-source-information-architecture-design-using-the-tools-you-have-to-conduct-card-sorting-and-tree-testing
- [statement] Analyze repeated groupings and labels, using similarity matrices to inspect co-grouping. Keep audience differences visible: ONRR normalized equivalent category names and examined its two user types separately. (medium confidence) — https://raw.studio/blog/card-sorting-and-tree-testing · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://digital.gov/2022/01/06/open-source-information-architecture-design-using-the-tools-you-have-to-conduct-card-sorting-and-tree-testing
- [statement] Report success and path directness separately. Success concerns reaching the correct destination; directness concerns avoiding detours or backtracking. High eventual success can conceal difficult paths. (medium confidence) — https://raw.studio/blog/card-sorting-and-tree-testing · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/interpreting-tree-test-results/
- [statement] Define acceptable destinations for each task before calculating tree-test success. Inspect failed destinations and paths as well as successful ones: NN/G notes that a participant can confidently choose a wrong destination without backtracking. (low confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/interpreting-tree-test-results/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing
- [statement] Write realistic tree-test tasks without repeating category labels that give away the answer. Pilot the wording before the main study to detect ambiguity and priming. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/tree-testing/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://digital.gov/2022/01/06/open-source-information-architecture-design-using-the-tools-you-have-to-conduct-card-sorting-and-tree-testing
- [statement] Small qualitative tree tests can explain confusing labels, while quantitative comparisons require larger samples and attention to uncertainty. NN/G recommends comparing alternative trees using the same tasks and considering confidence intervals and statistical significance. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/tree-testing/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/interpreting-tree-test-results/
- [statement] A closed-card-sort resampling study found that estimated sample requirements depended on whether agreement was assessed through co-occurrence matrices or clustering similarity. Its authors identify a gender-skewed sample, a single tool and absent qualitative reasoning data as limitations; its findings should not be treated as a universal recruitment threshold. (low confidence) — https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3749012.3749050 · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing
- [statement] Do not expect a single broad card sort to solve findability. Sam Ng reports that mixing content granularity and market segments made earlier sorts difficult to manage; NN/G likewise says users may group the same content differently and final navigation decisions need judgment and additional research. (medium confidence) — https://www.uxmatters.com/mt/archives/2007/09/card-sorting-mistakes-made-and-lessons-learned.php · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/card-sorting-tree-testing-differences/
- [statement] Interpret success together with directness and paths: eventual success may require backtracking, and a direct path can also end at a wrong destination. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/interpreting-tree-test-results/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/tree-testing/
- [statement] Separate exploratory diagnosis from population estimates: a small qualitative tree test can reveal confusing labels, but quantitative success-rate estimates require a larger sample selected for the desired precision. (medium confidence) — https://www.nngroup.com/articles/tree-testing/ · keywords: Information architecture, card sorting and tree testing · also: https://measuringu.com/tree-testing-ia/
